body_html:
Place value to 10 000

A 4-digit number has thousands, hundreds, tens and ones. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right. 10 ones make 1 ten, 10 tens make 1 hundred, 10 hundreds make 1 thousand, and 10 thousands make 10 000 (ten thousand).

Base ten blocks show the value of each place. Count each kind of block and write a digit for it.

Place value discs show the same idea. Find the value of each group of discs, then add.

Reading and writing numbers in words

Read the thousands first and say “thousand”. Then read the hundreds, tens and ones. If a place has 0, do not say it, but always write the 0.

NumeralsWords
4053four thousand and fifty-three
2605two thousand, six hundred and five
7008seven thousand and eight
10 000ten thousand
Words to numerals

Write six thousand and seven in numerals.

six thousand → 6; then three more digits for hundreds, tens and ones: 007.

Answer: 6007 (not 607)

Value of a digit and expanded form

The digit is the symbol. Its value depends on its place. In 3785 the digit 7 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 700, not 7.

Expanded form shows the value of every digit: 6208 = 6000 + 200 + 8.

Comparing and ordering

First count the digits: a 4-digit number is greater than any 3-digit number. If the numbers have the same number of digits, compare place by place from the left until two digits are different.

Compare

3056 ☐ 3065

Thousands: 3 = 3. Hundreds: 0 = 0. Tens: 5 < 6.

Answer: 3056 < 3065

Number patterns

To count on in hundreds, add 1 to the hundreds digit. To count on in thousands, add 1 to the thousands digit. When the hundreds go past 9, rename 10 hundreds as 1 thousand.

Count on in hundreds

4700, 4800, 4900, ☐

4900 + 100: 9 hundreds + 1 hundred = 10 hundreds = 1 thousand.

Answer: 5000

In word problems, draw a bar model to see what to find.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Leaving out zeros (four thousand and fifty-three → 453)Write three digits after the thousands: 4 | 053 → 4053
Saying “zero hundred” (four thousand, zero hundred and fifty-three)Leave out places with 0: four thousand and fifty-three
Giving the digit, not its value (the 7 in 3785 is 7)It is in the hundreds place: 700
Counting the blocks or discs (3 + 2 + 1 = 6)Add the values: 3000 + 20 + 1 = 3021
Comparing the first digits only (999 > 1002)Count the digits first: 1002 > 999
Forgetting to rename in a pattern (4900 + 100 → 4000)10 hundreds make 1 thousand: 5000

faq.q: What is taught in P3 whole numbers?
faq.a: Primary 3 students count in hundreds and thousands, read and write numbers up to 10 000 in numerals and in words, find the value of each digit, compare and order numbers, and continue number patterns.

faq.q: How do you write four thousand and fifty-three in numerals?
faq.a: Write 4 for the thousands, then three more digits for hundreds, tens and ones: 4053. The 0 holds the empty hundreds place, so it is not 453.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with numbers to 10 000?
faq.a: The most common mistake is leaving out zeros, such as writing 4053 as 453. Another is giving the digit instead of its value: the 7 in 3785 is worth 700.

faq.q: Is numbers to 10 000 in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Numbers up to 10 000, including place value, reading and writing, comparing and ordering, and number patterns, are part of Whole Numbers in the MOE 2021 Primary 3 Mathematics syllabus.

sets.title: Place value with base ten blocks and discs

items.e: Find the value of each group of blocks: 2 × 1000 = 2000; 3 × 100 = 300; 4 × 10 = 40; 5 × 1 = 5. Add them: 2345. Do not just count the blocks: a thousand cube is worth 1000.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands. In 5824 the red 5 is in the thousands place.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group of discs: 3 × 1000 = 3000; 2 × 100 = 200. Add them: 3200. There are no tens or ones, so write 0 in those places. Do not just count the discs: each disc has its own value.

items.q: How many hundreds make 1000?
items.e: Count in hundreds: 100, 200, 300 … 1000. That is 10 hundreds. Each place is worth 10 times the place to its right.

items.q: What number does the place value chart show?
items.e: Read the digits from the thousands to the ones: 4, 0, 5, 3. Keep every 0: it holds an empty place. The number is 4053.

Find the value of each group of blocks: 1 × 1000 = 1000; 4 × 100 = 400. Add them: 1400. There are no tens or ones, so write 0 in those places. Do not just count the blocks: a thousand cube is worth 1000.

items.q: In 3816, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: In 3816: thousands 3, hundreds 8, tens 1, ones 6. The hundreds digit is 8.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group of discs: 2 × 1000 = 2000; 4 × 10 = 40; 1 × 1 = 1. Add them: 2041. There are no hundreds, so write 0 in that place. Do not just count the discs: each disc has its own value.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands. In 7391 the red 3 is in the hundreds place.

items.q: What is the greatest 4-digit number?
items.e: Put the greatest digit, 9, in all 4 places: 9999. 10 000 has 5 digits and 999 has only 3.

Find the value of each group of blocks: 3 × 1000 = 3000; 2 × 10 = 20; 6 × 1 = 6. Add them: 3026. There are no hundreds, so write 0 in that place. Do not just count the blocks: a thousand cube is worth 1000.

items.q: What number does the place value chart show?
items.e: Read the digits from the thousands to the ones: 7, 0, 0, 8. Keep every 0: it holds an empty place. The number is 7008.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group of discs: 1 × 1000 = 1000; 3 × 1 = 3. Add them: 1003. There are no hundreds or tens, so write 0 in those places. Do not just count the discs: each disc has its own value.

items.q: In 9274, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: In 9274: thousands 9, hundreds 2, tens 7, ones 4. The tens digit is 7.

items.q: What is the smallest 4-digit number?
items.e: A 4-digit number cannot start with 0, so put 1 in the thousands place and 0 in the other places: 1000. 999 has only 3 digits.

Find the value of each group of blocks: 2 × 1000 = 2000; 7 × 1 = 7. Add them: 2007. There are no hundreds or tens, so write 0 in those places. Do not just count the blocks: a thousand cube is worth 1000.

items.q: Which place is the red digit in?
items.e: Read the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands. In 4567 the red 6 is in the tens place.

items.q: What number do the place value discs show?
items.e: Find the value of each group of discs: 4 × 1000 = 4000; 1 × 100 = 100; 3 × 1 = 3. Add them: 4103. There are no tens, so write 0 in that place. Do not just count the discs: each disc has its own value.

Find the value of each group of blocks: 1 × 1000 = 1000; 5 × 100 = 500; 6 × 10 = 60. Add them: 1560. There are no ones, so write 0 in that place. Do not just count the blocks: a thousand cube is worth 1000.

items.q: What number is 1 more than 9999?
items.e: 9999 + 1: every 9 becomes 0 as you rename, and a 1 goes in the ten thousands place: 10 000 (ten thousand). (9998 is 1 less, and 100 000 has too many zeros.)

sets.title: Reading and writing numbers in words

items.q: How do you write 3000 in words?
items.e: 3000 is 3 thousands, so we say “three thousand”. Three thousand is 3000; thirty thousand would be 30 000.

items.q: How do you write 4053 in words?
c: four thousand, five hundred and three
four thousand, zero hundred and fifty-three
items.e: Read place by place: 4 thousands → four thousand; 0 hundreds → say nothing; 53 → fifty-three. So 4053 is “four thousand and fifty-three”. We never say “zero hundred”. Just leave the hundreds out.

items.q: Which number is four thousand and fifty-three?
items.e: Write the thousands digit, then always three more digits for hundreds, tens and ones: 4 thousands → 4; fifty-three → 053. So the number is 4053. 453 leaves out the 0 that holds the hundreds place.

items.q: Which number is seven thousand and eight?
items.e: Write the thousands digit, then always three more digits for hundreds, tens and ones: 7 thousands → 7; eight → 008. So the number is 7008. 78 and 708 leave out zeros that hold empty places.

items.q: How do you write 6705 in words?
c: six thousand, seven hundred and five
six thousand, seven hundred and fifty
items.e: Read place by place: 6 thousands → six thousand; 7 hundreds → seven hundred; 5 → five. So 6705 is “six thousand, seven hundred and five”. The 0 tens are not said, but the 0 is still written.

items.q: 5300 = five thousand, ☐ hundred. Which word goes in the box?
items.e: Read place by place: 5 thousands → five thousand; 3 hundreds → three hundred. So 5300 is “five thousand, three hundred”.

items.q: Which number is two thousand, six hundred?
items.e: Write the thousands digit, then always three more digits for hundreds, tens and ones: 2 thousands → 2; six hundred → 600. So the number is 2600.

items.q: How do you write 2410 in words?
c: two thousand, one hundred and forty
two thousand, four hundred and ten
two thousand, four hundred and one
items.e: Read place by place: 2 thousands → two thousand; 4 hundreds → four hundred; 10 → ten. So 2410 is “two thousand, four hundred and ten”.

items.q: Which number is five thousand and forty?
items.e: Write the thousands digit, then always three more digits for hundreds, tens and ones: 5 thousands → 5; forty → 040. So the number is 5040.

items.q: Which number is read without the word “hundred”?
items.e: 3045 has 0 in the hundreds place, so we do not say “hundred”: three thousand and forty-five. The others: 3450 is three thousand, four hundred and fifty; 3504 is three thousand, five hundred and four; 3405 is three thousand, four hundred and five.

items.q: How do you write 8090 in words?
items.e: Read place by place: 8 thousands → eight thousand; 0 hundreds → say nothing; 90 → ninety. So 8090 is “eight thousand and ninety”. The 9 is in the tens place, so we say “ninety”.

items.q: Which number is three thousand, nine hundred and twelve?
items.e: Write the thousands digit, then always three more digits for hundreds, tens and ones: 3 thousands → 3; nine hundred and twelve → 912. So the number is 3912. Do not write “thousand” as 000 before the 912: the number has only 4 digits.

items.q: Siti writes “six thousand and seven” as 607. What should she write?
items.e: Six thousand → 6. Then three more digits: no hundreds, no tens, 7 ones → 007. 6 | 007 = 6007. 607 is only six hundred and seven: Siti left out a zero.

items.q: How do you write 1515 in words?
c: one thousand, five hundred and fifteen
five thousand, one hundred and fifteen
one thousand, five hundred and five
one thousand, five hundred and fifty
items.e: Read place by place: 1 thousand → one thousand; 5 hundreds → five hundred; 15 → fifteen. So 1515 is “one thousand, five hundred and fifteen”. The last two digits are 15: fifteen, not fifty.

items.q: 2050 = two thousand and ☐. Which word goes in the box?
items.e: Read place by place: 2 thousands → two thousand; 0 hundreds → say nothing; 50 → fifty. So 2050 is “two thousand and fifty”.

items.q: Which number is eight thousand, eight hundred and eighteen?
items.e: Write the thousands digit, then always three more digits for hundreds, tens and ones: 8 thousands → 8; eight hundred and eighteen → 818. So the number is 8818. Eighteen is 18; eighty is 80.

items.q: How do you write 9006 in words?
items.e: Read place by place: 9 thousands → nine thousand; 0 hundreds → say nothing; 6 → six. So 9006 is “nine thousand and six”.

items.q: Write nine thousand and nine in numerals. How many zeros does it have?
items.e: Nine thousand and nine is 9009: 9 thousands, 0 hundreds, 0 tens, 9 ones. It has 2 zeros. (909 has only 1 zero and is nine hundred and nine.)

items.q: Which number is six thousand and nineteen?
items.e: Write the thousands digit, then always three more digits for hundreds, tens and ones: 6 thousands → 6; nineteen → 019. So the number is 6019. Nineteen is 19; ninety is 90.

items.q: How do you write 10 000 in words?
items.e: 10 000 is 10 thousands, so we say “ten thousand”. It is 1 more than 9999.

sets.title: Value of a digit and expanded form

items.q: What is the value of the 7 in 3785?
items.e: The 7 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 7 hundreds = 700. The digit is 7, but its value is 700.

items.q: What is the value of the 5 in 5246?
items.e: The 5 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 5 thousands = 5000. The digit is 5, but its value is 5000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 4 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 4 thousands = 4000. The digit is 4, but its value is 4000.

items.q: 4503 = 4000 + ☐ + 3. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 4503 = 4000 + 500 + 3. The 5 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 500.

items.q: What is the value of the 3 in 9431?
items.e: The 3 is in the tens place, so it is worth 3 tens = 30. The digit is 3, but its value is 30.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 5 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 5 hundreds = 500. The digit is 5, but its value is 500.

items.q: In 2837, the digit 3 stands for ☐.
items.e: Count the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands. The 3 is in the tens place, so it stands for 3 tens = 30.

items.q: What number is 3000 + 400 + 5?
items.e: Put each value in its place: 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens, 5 ones → 3405.

items.q: What is the value of the 8 in 6812?
items.e: The 8 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 8 hundreds = 800. The digit is 8, but its value is 800.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 6 is in the tens place, so it is worth 6 tens = 60. The digit is 6, but its value is 60.

items.q: Which shows 6208 in expanded form?
items.e: Write the value of each digit: 6 thousands = 6000, 2 hundreds = 200, 0 tens, 8 ones = 8. So 6208 = 6000 + 200 + 8. The 0 tens is left out.

items.q: What number is 9000 + 80 + 1?
items.e: 9 thousands, 0 hundreds, 8 tens, 1 one → 9081. Write 0 in the empty hundreds place.

items.q: In 6452, the digit 6 stands for ☐.
items.e: Count the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands. The 6 is in the thousands place, so it stands for 6 thousands = 6000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 2 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 2 hundreds = 200. The digit is 2, but its value is 200.

items.q: 7024 = 7000 + ☐ + 4. What number goes in the box?
items.e: The 2 is in the tens place, so its value is 20. 7000 + 20 + 4 = 7024.

items.q: 3400 = ☐ hundreds. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 3400 = 34 × 100, so it is 34 hundreds. (3000 is 30 hundreds, plus 4 hundreds.)
2 × 1000 = 2000, 6 × 100 = 600, 4 × 1 = 4. Add them: 2604. There are no tens, so the tens digit is 0.

items.q: In which number is the digit 6 worth 600?
items.e: The 6 must be in the hundreds place (the 3rd digit from the right). In 4632 the 6 is worth 600. In 6432 it is worth 6000, in 4362 it is worth 60 and in 4326 it is worth 6.

items.q: How many tens are there in 2500?
items.e: 2500 = 250 × 10, so there are 250 tens. (25 is the number of hundreds.)

items.q: What number is 12 hundreds?
items.e: 12 hundreds = 10 hundreds + 2 hundreds = 1000 + 200 = 1200. Rename 10 hundreds as 1 thousand.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 3 tens is more than 0 tens. So 5430 > 5403.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1002 has 4 digits and 999 has only 3, so 1002 is greater. A big first digit does not matter when a number has fewer digits.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 6 hundreds is more than 5 hundreds. So 2645 > 2546. 2645 is the greatest.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 6 tens is more than 5 tens. So 3065 > 3056.

items.q: Which number is between 4590 and 4610?
items.e: 4590 < 4600 < 4610. 4509 is less than 4590, 4690 is more than 4610, and 460 has only 3 digits.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: 999 has only 3 digits. The other numbers have 4 digits, so 999 is the least, even though it starts with 9.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. Start with the thousands: 8 thousands is more than 7 thousands. So 8001 > 7999.

items.q: Put 4530, 4350, 4503 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: All have 4 thousands. Hundreds: 3 < 5, so 4350 is the least. 4530 and 4503 both have 5 hundreds. Tens: 0 < 3, so 4503 < 4530. Order: 4350, 4503, 4530.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 6 hundreds is more than 0 hundreds. So 6600 > 6060.

items.q: Use each of the digits 3, 8, 1 and 6 once. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Put the greatest digit in the thousands place, then the next greatest, and so on: 8, 6, 3, 1. The greatest number is 8631.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 9 tens is more than 0 tens. So 6890 > 6809. 6890 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is greater than 8900 but less than 9000?
items.e: 8950 has 8 thousands and 9 hundreds, so it is between 8900 and 9000. 9850 and 9050 are more than 9000; 895 is less than 8900.

items.q: Put 1201, 1210, 1120 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: All have 1 thousand. Hundreds: 1 < 2, so 1120 is the least. 1210 and 1201 both have 2 hundreds. Tens: 1 > 0, so 1210 > 1201. Order: 1210, 1201, 1120.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 8 tens is more than 7 tens. So 4587 > 4578.

items.q: Use each of the digits 5, 0, 7 and 2 once. What is the smallest 4-digit number you can make?
items.e: A 4-digit number cannot start with 0. Put the smallest other digit first: 2. Then 0, 5, 7: 2057. (0257 is just 257, which has only 3 digits.)

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 2 hundreds is more than 1 hundred. So 3152 < 3215. 3152 is the least.

items.q: Put 9900, 10 000, 9090, 990 in order from least to greatest.
items.e: 990 has only 3 digits, so it is the least. 10 000 has 5 digits, so it is the greatest. 9090 < 9900 (hundreds: 0 < 9). Order: 990, 9090, 9900, 10 000.

items.q: What is the greatest 4-digit number that is less than 5000?
items.e: Go back 1 from 5000: 4999. 5001 is more than 5000, 4000 is not the greatest, and 499 has only 3 digits.

items.q: Use each of the digits 4, 0, 9 and 0 once. What is the greatest number you can make?
items.e: Put the greatest digits first: 9 in the thousands place, 4 in the hundreds place, then the two 0s: 9400.

items.q: Put 6066, 6606, 6660, 6006 in order from greatest to least.
items.e: All have 6 thousands. Hundreds: 6660 and 6606 have 6 hundreds; the others have 0. 6660 and 6606: tens 6 > 0, so 6660 > 6606. 6066 and 6006: tens 6 > 0, so 6066 > 6006. Order: 6660, 6606, 6066, 6006.

items.q:
What is the next number in the pattern?
2400, 3400, 4400, ☐
items.e: Each number is 1000 more: the thousands digit goes up by 1. 4400 + 1000 = 5400. (4500 adds only 100.)

items.q:
What is the next number in the pattern?
1570, 1670, 1770, ☐
items.e: Each number is 100 more: the hundreds digit goes up by 1. 1770 + 100 = 1870. (2770 adds 1000, and 1780 adds 10.)

items.q: What number is 100 more than 3960?
items.e: 3960 + 100: 9 hundreds + 1 hundred = 10 hundreds. Rename them as 1 thousand: 3 thousands become 4. 3960 + 100 = 4060. (4960 adds 1000, and 3970 adds 10.)

items.q:
What is the next number in the pattern?
8360, 7360, 6360, ☐
items.e: Each number is 1000 less: the thousands digit goes down by 1. 6360 − 1000 = 5360. (6260 takes away only 100.)

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 3000 to 4000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 100. The arrow is 2 spaces after 3500: 3600, 3700. (3070 counts each space as 10.)

items.q:
What is the next number in the pattern?
3200, 3100, 3000, ☐
items.e: Each number is 100 less. 3000 − 100 = 2900: rename 1 thousand as 10 hundreds, then take away 1 hundred. (2000 takes away 1000.)

items.q: What number is 1000 less than 10 000?
items.e: 10 000 is 10 thousands. Take away 1 thousand: 9 thousands = 9000. (9900 takes away only 100.)

items.q:
What is the missing number?
6180, ☐, 8180, 9180
items.e: From 8180 to 9180 is 1000 more, so the rule is “add 1000”. 6180 + 1000 = 7180.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 10 000 there are 10 equal spaces, so each space is 1000. The arrow is 2 spaces after 5000: 6000, 7000. (700 counts each space as 100.)

items.q:
What is the next number in the pattern?
4700, 4800, 4900, ☐
items.e: Each number is 100 more. 4900 + 100 = 5000: 10 hundreds are renamed as 1 thousand. (4000 forgets to rename.)

items.q:
What is the rule for this pattern?
5630, 5430, 5230, 5030
items.e: The numbers get smaller, so we subtract. 5630 − 5430 = 200. The hundreds digit goes down by 2 each time. The rule is “subtract 200”.

items.q:
What is the missing number?
9450, 9350, ☐, 9150
items.e: Each number is 100 less: 9450, 9350, 9250, 9150. Only the hundreds digit changes. (8250 takes away 1000 instead of 100.)

items.q: Ali’s school has 1245 students. Mei Ling’s school has 1254 students. Which is true?
c: You cannot tell which school has more
Both schools have the same number of students
Mei Ling’s school has more students
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 5 tens is more than 4 tens. So 1254 > 1245. Mei Ling’s school has more students.

items.q: The school library has 4680 books. It gets 100 new books every month. How many books will it have after 3 months?
items.e: Count on in hundreds 3 times: 4780, 4880, 4980. (4780 is after only 1 month, and 7680 adds 3 thousands.)

items.q: Hafiz counts back in thousands: 9200, 8200, … What is the 4th number he says?
items.e: 9200 (1st), 8200 (2nd), 7200 (3rd), 6200 (4th). Each time the thousands digit goes down by 1. (8900 counts back in hundreds.)

items.q: For a recycling drive, Class A collected 3850 cans. Class B collected 1000 more cans than Class A. How many cans did Class B collect?
items.e: Class B’s bar is Class A’s bar plus 1000. 3850 + 1000 = 4850: the thousands digit goes up by 1. (2850 subtracts, and 3950 adds only 100.)

items.q: Mrs Lim had $5000 in the bank. She took out $1000 every month for 3 months. How much money did she have left?
items.e: Count back in thousands 3 times: $4000, $3000, $2000. ($4997 takes away $3 instead of $3000.)

items.q: The zoo had 6430 visitors on Saturday and 5430 visitors on Friday. How many more visitors were there on Saturday?
items.e: The difference is the part marked ?. 6430 − 5430 = 1000: only the thousands digit is different (6 and 5). (11 860 adds the numbers.)

items.q: A shop had 7000 mandarin oranges for Chinese New Year. It sold 2000 of them. How many mandarin oranges were left?
items.e: The whole bar is 7000 and one part is 2000. 7000 − 2000 = 5000 (7 thousands − 2 thousands = 5 thousands). (9000 adds, and 6800 takes away only 200.)

items.q: A bakery sold 900 buns on Monday. Each day after that, it sold 100 more buns than the day before. How many buns did it sell on Friday?
items.e: Monday 900, Tuesday 1000, Wednesday 1100, Thursday 1200, Friday 1300. From Monday to Friday there are only 4 jumps of 100. (1400 adds 5 jumps.)
